scenes.head: The 6 families of NGX stocks
scenes.body: Hundreds of names, a few big families
scenes.line: Come sit down a minute for a quick money talk. When you open the Nigerian Exchange, it can look like hundreds of names. However, most of them fall into a few big families. Let's meet six.
scenes.img: Aerial view of the Lagos skyline at dusk with Marina and Broad Street office towers, cinematic

scenes.head: 1 & 2: Banks and insurers
scenes.body: They make money from money: lending, fees and premiums
scenes.line: First and second, the banks and the insurers. They make money from money: lending, fees, and insurance premiums. Many of them are popular with people who love dividends.
scenes.img: Interior of a modern Nigerian bank banking hall with customers and staff, clean, bright, no logos

scenes.head: 3: Industrial goods
scenes.line: Third, industrial goods. Think cement and building materials. When roads and houses are going up, these companies are busy.
scenes.img: A construction site in Abuja with cement bags, scaffolding and workers in hard hats, sunny day

scenes.head: 4: Consumer goods
scenes.body: The food, drinks and household things you buy every week
scenes.line: Fourth, consumer goods. The food, drinks and household things you buy every week. However, when prices rise faster than salaries, people buy less, and Mr. Inflation squeezes them.
scenes.img: A busy Nigerian supermarket aisle with shelves of food and drinks and a shopper with a basket, no brand names visible

scenes.head: 5 & 6: Oil and gas, telecoms
scenes.body: Energy, and the networks your phone runs on
scenes.line: Fifth and sixth, oil and gas, and telecoms. One moves energy, the other keeps your phone and data running. Some of the biggest companies on the exchange sit here.
scenes.img: Split scene of an offshore oil platform at sunset and a telecom mast in a Nigerian town, dramatic sky

scenes.head: Why the family matters
scenes.body: Each family reacts to different news
scenes.line: So, why does this matter? Each family reacts to different news. Interest rates move the banks, building moves cement, and oil prices move energy. Know the family, and the moves make more sense.
scenes.img: A Nigerian woman analyst looking at a large screen of market charts in a calm trading room, thoughtful

scenes.head: Know the stock before you buy the story.
scenes.body: One plain-English money lesson every weekday at moloneystreetre.com
scenes.line: One simple money lesson every weekday on moloneystreetre.com. Know the stock before you buy the story. See you on Moloney Street.
